 (10) Clear the ADS, go back to the calibration tab and click load existing calibration
 (11) Browse to the .prm created `save_dir\User\texture30_PR\Calibration\ENGINX_193749_Texture30.prm`
 (12) Repeat steps (2-9)

title: Split Activation Fit function into two seperate functions
body:
Description of work.
 Split the Activation Fitting function for Muons into two separate functions, one for Kelvin and one for meV.
 

 To test:
 

 1. Enable the model analysis tab and plot (see #32572 for details on how to do this)
 3. Open Muon Analysis GUI
 4. Change Instrument to EMU
 5. Load runs 20901-18
 6. Go to the Grouping Tab
 7. Guess Alpha
 8. Go to fitting tab and add a DynamicKuboToyabe Fitting Function
 9. Fix the Field to 0, and set Delta to 0.35 and Nu to 0.01
 10. Go to the Sequential Fitting Tab and select runs 20901-17 and then sequentially fit selected
 11. Go to the Results Tab
 12. Select Temp_Sample from the log results and then click Output Results
 13. Open the Model fitting tab and change x axis to Temp_sample and y axis to Nu
 14. Add an ActivationK Fit Function and fit (leave Unit as K). AttemptRate = 33.4 +- 3.6 us^-1 and Barrier = 589.7+-13.9 and ChiSquared should be about 3.75 or better.
 

 Note:
 We have not been provided with data in meV to be able to directly test ActivationmeV fitting function. However as the conversion from Kelvin to meV is provided by https://github.com/mantidproject/mantid/blob/15ef1d68a3427cf52dbf91faa2072ca5c5bae02d/Framework/Kernel/inc/MantidKernel/PhysicalConstants.h#L63 which is already tested and the above tests the other part of the functionality ActivationmeV uses then provided the above functional test works, the code is reviewed and all the CI tests pass then ActivationmeV should be good to go.
 

 Fixes #33090.

title: Extend guess range outside of data range in Muon analysis
body:
Description of work.
 

 This PR adds the ability to plot the fit guess outside of the range of the data in muon analysis.
 

 To test:
 1. Open muon analysis.
 2. load MUSR 62260-3
 3. go to fitting
 4. add gausosc function
 5. check plot guess by default it plots using the same range as the data
 6. in the fit options change the `plot guess using` to x at data points. this allows you to chane the number of points to be used in the guess workspace
 7. chane the number of points and the plot will update.
 8. change the `plot guess using` to custom x range, this allows you to change the start_x and end_x as well as the number of points in the guess
 9. change the start_x and end_x and see the plot update.
 10. fit the function
 11. got to results and create a results table,
 12. go to model fitting, and repete the same steps as for the fitting tab. all the plot guess options should work the same.

Description of work.
 Added a new Activation Fit function for Muon modelling and associated documentation.

title: Add Sample Geometry to Batch File
body:
Description of work.
 This adds sample thickness, height, and width information to the SANS batch files.
 When loading a batch file, the table will be populated with the sample geometry values if there are present in the batch file, or will default to using file information if not (current behaviour).
 Additionally, exporting the SANS table as a batch file will include the sample geometries
 

 Report to: Steve King ISIS
 

 To test:
 1. Interfaces -> SANS -> ISIS SANS
 2. Load the attached batch file (`Load Batch File`)
 3. Click `Sample Geometry` checkbox at the bottom of the gui. This will show the sample geometry values in the table.
 4. The Sample Thickness, Sample Height, Sample Width values should be 2.0, 8.0, 8.0, respectively. These are the default values taken from file information
 5. Change these values in the table
 6. Click the export table button (rightmost button in the row of buttons above the table) and save the table
 7. Open the csv you just saved in your favourite csv reading software. The row should contain sample geometry keys with the values you input
 8. Back on the SANS gui, select the row and click the remove row button
 9. Then click `Load Batch File` again and select the file you saved. The sample geometries should be the values you set before exporting the table 
 

 Fixes #25932

title: Extend attenuation correction in AnvredCorrection higher muR
body:
Description of work.
 Have extended the attenuation correction to higher muR by fitting function ln(A) to a polynmial as a function of muR at fixed theta (as done in [1]) - but using the tabulated A* values (A* = 1/A) from [2] which goes to higher muR.
 

 This appears to have also fixed a bug - as the agreement with the Monte-Carlo is much better now...
 

 ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/55979119/140786164-90aca104-adba-4738-88b0-a4cb056d3dec.png)
 

 

 The correction factor to apply is now found by interpolation of A (rather than A*) as recommended in [1]. In addition I have replaced the linear interpolation with interpolation using the Eq.
 `A(th) = L0 + L1*(sin(th)^2)`
 This captures better the smooth variation of the `A(th)` and exhibits roughly the right functional form (especially at low muR). Indeed in [1] they suggest that it is possible to fit ` A(th) = sum_{i=0}^{6} L_i *(sin(th)^(2i))`.
 I've confirmed that this does indeed work better (see green markers in residual plot), below I interpolate using fit parameters from `theta +/- 5 deg` from the black data points at three theta values.
  
 ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/55979119/140897446-4db7b6cf-0925-446e-a177-9145bcaa1815.png)
 

 

 To test:
 

 (1) Check that the values of Astar agree with the tabulated values in [2]. Choose some theta and muR values to check from table and put them in the variables of this script. Try muR > 2.5 (i.e. greater than previous limit). 
 

 ```
 theta = 50
 muR = 1
 CreateSampleWorkspace(OutputWorkspace='ws', Function='Powder Diffraction', 
  XMin=2000, XMax=20000, BinWidth=200, NumBanks=1, BankPixelWidth=1, PixelSpacing=0.02,
  WorkspaceType="Histogram")
 EditInstrumentGeometry(Workspace='ws', L2=0.5, Polar=2*theta)
 ConvertUnits(InputWorkspace='ws', OutputWorkspace='ws', Target='Wavelength')
 # 1 cm sphere
 shape = '''<sphere id="V-sphere">
  <centre x="0.0" y="0.0" z="0.0" />
  <radius val="0.01"/>
  </sphere>'''
 SetSample('ws', Geometry={'Shape': 'CSG', 'Value': shape})
 SetSampleMaterial('ws', SampleNumberDensity=1.0,
  ScatteringXSection = muR, AttenuationXSection=0.0, ChemicalFormula='V') 
 wsphere = SphericalAbsorption(InputWorkspace='ws', OutputWorkspace='attenuation_SphericalAbsorption')
 w = MonteCarloAbsorption(InputWorkspace='ws', OutputWorkspace='attenuation_MonteCarlo', EventsPerPoint=5000)
 

 Astar_sphere = 1/wsphere.readY(0)[0]
 Astar_mc = 1/w.readY(0)[0]
 print(Astar_sphere, Astar_mc) # compare this with Dwiggins
 ```
 

 The values should be within <~ 0.5% of the Weber values [2] for most theta and muR (and indeed consistent within the errorbars of the monte-carlo).
 

 There should be a warning if muR > 9 and the result won't agree as well with the Monte-Carlo particularly at large theta (however for neutrons samples rarely have muR>3).
 

 (2) Test the interpolation by picking a theta that isn't a multiple of 5 - it should still be consistent with the Monte-Carlo 
 

 (3) Try adding a finite absorption cross-section to compare the Monte-Carlo curve to the `SphericalAbsorption`. Note the latter is a histogram, so plot it first and turn off normalisation (right-click on axes -> Normalisation -> None) before overplotting the Monte-Carlo curve (or plot using this script).

title: Use property manager in batch algorithm runner
body:
Note that this work is by @DavidFair and @ConorMFinn rather than myself.
 

 This PR makes changes to the BatchAlgorithmRunner and related classes to change from using AlgorithmRuntimeProps which was previously a map of string to string, to using the property manager so that we can set proper property types. This is required for upstream work in the reflectometry GUI which will need to pass workspaces as pointers rather than string names, because they will not be in the ADS.

 - Test something in Indirect (from their testing instructions) still works

title: Add units for fit parameters to model fitting

title: Add algorithm to sum banks for ISIS Reflectometry
body:
Description of work.
 

 This PR adds an algorithm to do the first steps of reduction from an ISIS Reflectometry 2D detector to sum across banks from a region of interest into a single bank.
 

 This uses SmoothNeighbours to do the summing. Some minor changes were required to get this to work with INTER data:
  - Ignore slits and supermirrors in `containsRectDetectors` because they were causing the instrument to be incorrectly identified as non-rectangular.
  - Add a flag to `getDetectorIDToWorkspaceIndexMap` to ignore invalid detector IDs. This was causing an error due to having multiple detectors per spectrum, but this is irrelevant in our case where those are invalid detectors which will be ignored anyway.
 

 To test:
 

 - Download the input workspace here (note that this has had an experimental IDF applied to it).
  - [INTER45455_inst.zip](https://github.com/mantidproject/mantid/files/7453399/INTER45455_inst.zip)
 - Run the script below. Note that the first two lines execute the new algorithm. The rest is a comparison with the same calculation done using GroupDetectors.
 - Check that the CompareWorkspaces call at the end outputs the text `The workspaces "INTER45455_summedX" and "Inter45455_SummedX_GroupDets" matched!` in the log.
 

 ```
 ws=Load('INTER45455_inst.nxs', OutputWorkspace='INTER45455')
 ReflectometryISISSumBanks(InputWorkspace='INTER45455', OutputWorkspace='INTER45455_summedX', ROIDetectorIDs='2061-2180')
 

 #
 # Manual check against sum in X using GroupDetectors
 #
 start_idx, end_idx = 65, 184 # ws idx for our start/end det ID
 npixels=ws.getInstrument().getComponentByName('linear-detector').ypixels()
 groups = [""] * npixels
 for ws_idx in range(ws.getNumberHistograms()):
  if ws_idx < start_idx or ws_idx > end_idx:
  continue
  # Work out which output pixel to sum the input pixel into
  bank = math.ceil(ws_idx / npixels)
  pixel = ws_idx - bank * npixels
  # Create a grouping pattern to do the sum for each output pixel
  groups[pixel] = groups[pixel] + str(ws_idx) + '+'
 # Create the final grouping pattern to do all the sums
 grouping = ', '.join(groups)
 GroupDetectors(InputWorkspace=ws, OutputWorkspace='Inter45455_SummedX_GroupDets', GroupingPattern=grouping, Behaviour='Sum')
 CompareWorkspaces(Workspace1='INTER45455_summedX', Workspace2='Inter45455_SummedX_GroupDets', CheckSpectraMap=False, CheckInstrument=False, CheckSample=True, ToleranceRelErr=True, CheckAllData=True)
 ```
 

 This sums the middle two banks pixel-by-pixel into a single bank. Sliceviewer plots of the original and summed workspaces should look as follows:
 

 Before:
 

 ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12895056/139676374-2e010dfb-770e-4685-a255-0a49b3c47348.png)
 

 After:
 

 ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12895056/139676420-e301e3d2-f55a-4f59-befb-9436e3484b01.png)
 

 Fixes #32771

body:
Description of work.
 Added a new Muonium-style decoupling curve Fit function for Muon modelling, a test and associated documentation. This is part of the WIMDA project.
 

 To test:
 

 1. Open the ALC Interface
 2. Choose ```HIFI``` from the Instrument List
 3. Load runs 116860-116875
 4. Choose ```sample_magn_field``` for the Log value
 5. For the Dead Time Correction choose ```From Data File```
 6. Press ```Load```
 7. Once the runs have loaded press ```Baseline modelling``` button.
 8. Right click in the function box, choose ```Add function``` and select ```FlatBackground```
 9. Leave ```A0``` as 0 but right click and fix this parameter
 10. Add the ```MuoniumDecouplingCuve``` Function
 11. Set the parameters as follows:-
 - RepolarisingAsymmetry = 0.1
 - DecouplingField = 1000.0
 - BackgroundAsymmetry = 0.1
 12. Right click in Sections to Add a section (the default of 100 - 400 should be fine)
 13. Click Fit
 14. The parameters should change to approximately the following (they may be rounded up):-
 - RepolarisingAsymmetry = 0.21696513499545084  
 - DecouplingField = 985.588123668601
 - BackgroundAsymmetry = 0.04256004047828176

body:
Description of work.
 

 The file filter on the Fitting tab now includes the types Texture, Cropped and Custom
 Also Fixed a bug I found where if the Unit Filter was set to All and the Region of Interest (calibration type) combo box was set to something else like North, then no files were found, rather than bank_1 for dSpacing and TOF.
 

 To test:
 - Open the engineering diffraction interface
 - (Skip this section if you already have appropriately focused data) Create Focussed data for the region of interest as Texture, Cropped and Custom. To do this:
  - "Create New calibration" with the Calibration sample `ENGINX00305738.nxs`
  - Tick Crop Calibration, and choose Texture, Cropped ( I chose spectra 12-15) or Custom CalFile (use the cal file `ExternalData\Testing\Data\SystemTest\EnginX_NorthBank.cal`)
  - Click `Calibrate`
  - Move to the focus tab and use the Sample run: `ENGINX00305761.nxs` and Vanadium: `ENGINX00307521.nxs`
  - Repeat the above steps to produce focussed data for Texture, Cropped and Custom
 - In the fitting tab the Browse filters for unit and region of interest(calibration type) filter the files that appear when the browse button is clicked. Change the region of interest combobox from `All` to `Texture` and click browse. You should see only files that have texture and TOF in them. Exit the file browser and try this again for Custom and Cropped focus files.

Set the plot in the EngDiff fitting tab to 25% larger than the initial figure 
 unless the docked plot size is greater than this

 When the Engineering interface is opened the size of the plot window (bottom half of the fitting tab), that the plot exists within, is recorded. body:
Description of work.
 

 This PR fixes two problems in Muon Analysis.
 1. The List of results tables in model fitting was not being cleared when changing instruments
 2. Model fitting did not switch to the latest results table when added

 10. Go to results tab and create a results table called ResultsTable
 11. Go to Model fitting tab. You can see the plot contains the new table
 12. create a new results table called ResultsTable2
 13. go to Model fitting tab and see that ResultsTable2

title: Support rasterizing container with a different element size in MultipleScatteringCorrection and PaalmanPingsAbsorptionCorrection
body:
Description of work.
 

 <!-- If the original issue was raised by a user they should be named here. Do not leak email addresses
 Report to: [user name]
 -->
 

 - Original Gitlab user story: [PD377](https://code.ornl.gov/sns-hfir-scse/diffraction/powder/powder-diffraction/-/issues/377)
 - This is #32751 into `main`.
 

 Existing `MultipleScatteringCorrection` caches the cross term `L12` in memory, which can lead to a memory allocation error when the element size is very small (a common requirement for thin-wall containers).
 To circumvent this limitation, this PR allows users to use a different element size to rasterize the container so that the main sample can be rasterize with relatively larger element size, consequently reducing the memory pressure coming from caching `L12`.
 

 As an accompany change, the same feature is also introduced into `PaalmanPingsAbsorptionCorrection`.
 However, it is generally not necessary to specify a different element size in `PaalmanPingsAbsorptionCorrection` as it does not have second order absorption and the associated memory pressure from caching cross terms.
 

 To test:
 

 - Use the following script to create a fake instrument with only two detectors
 

 ```python
 from mantid.simpleapi import (
  ConvertUnits,
  CreateSampleWorkspace,
  EditInstrumentGeometry,
  SetSample,
  MultipleScatteringCorrection,
  PaalmanPingsAbsorptionCorrection,
  mtd,
 )
 

 # ----------------------- #
 # make an empty workspace #
 # ----------------------- #
 # Create a fake workspace with TOF data
 ws = CreateSampleWorkspace(Function='Powder Diffraction',
  NumBanks=2,
  BankPixelWidth=1,
  XUnit='TOF',
  XMin=1000,
  XMax=10000,)
 # Fake instrument
 EditInstrumentGeometry(ws,
  PrimaryFlightPath=5.0,
  SpectrumIDs=[1, 2],
  L2=[2.0, 2.0],
  Polar=[10.0, 90.0],
  Azimuthal=[0.0, 45.0],
  DetectorIDs=[1, 2],
  InstrumentName="Instrument")
 # set sample and container
 SetSample(
  ws,
  Geometry={
  "Shape": "Cylinder",
  "Center": [0., 0., 0.],
  "Height": 1.0, # cm
  "Radius": 0.3, # cm
  },
  Material = {
  "ChemicalFormula": "La-(B11)5.94-(B10)0.06",
  "SampleNumberDensity": 0.1,
  },
  ContainerMaterial = {
  "ChemicalFormula": "V",
  "SampleNumberDensity": 0.0721,
  },
  ContainerGeometry = {
  "Shape": "HollowCylinder",
  "Height": 1.0, # cm
  "InnerRadius": 0.3, # cm
  "OuterRadius": 0.35, # cm
  "Center": [0., 0., 0.],
  }
  )
 

 # to wavelength
 ConvertUnits(InputWorkspace=ws,
  OutputWorkspace=ws,
  Target="Wavelength",
  EMode="Elastic")
 ```
 

 - Use the following code to calculate the multiple scattering correction factor
 ```python
 MultipleScatteringCorrection(
  InputWorkspace = ws,
  Method="SampleAndContainer",
  ElementSize=0.5, # mm
  ContainerElementSize=0.1, # mm
  OutputWorkspace="rst",
  )
 ```
 

 - Use the following code to calculate the absorption correction with PaalmanPings formula
 ```python
 PaalmanPingsAbsorptionCorrection(
  InputWorkspace = ws,
  ElementSize=0.5,
  ContainerElementSize=0.1,
  OutputWorkspace="rst",
  )
 ```

title: Embed instrument viewer in refl gui
body:
Description of work.
 

 This PR embeds the instrument viewer display in the preview tab on the ISIS Reflectometry GUI.
 - An `InstViewModel` has been created to handle creating the instrument actor for the loaded workspace, and the surface to plot
 - The `PreviewPresenter` has handles both the synchronous case - where the workspace already exists in the ADS and can be plotted immediately - and the async case where it needs to be loaded via an algorithm.
 - `InstrumentActor` has been modified to take a message handler to handle pop-up messages rather than using QMessageBox itself. This is to avoid pop-up dialogs appearing when we are using `InstrumentActor` in unit tests.
 - A change to `GLDisplay` was required to ensure the instrument view plot is blank when first created, rather than just rendering what was on screen previously
 

 To test:
 

 - Open the ISIS Reflectometry interface and set instrument to INTER
 - Go to the Preview tab. The instrument viewer plot should be blank
 - Enter a run number for an unloaded workspace e.g. `13460` and press enter or click Load
 - The workspace should be displayed in the instrument plot
 - Load a different workspace into mantid separately and give it a different name e.g. INTER45455
 - Enter this name in the Preview tab and click load. This should use the workspace from the ADS rather than re-loading it. It should be displayed in the instrument view plot.
 

 - Also test the basic functionality of instrument viewer to check that nothing is broken

title: ISIS SANS - Standardise on front rear
body:
Description of work.
 The ISIS SANS Group has agreed to standardise on Front / Rear to replace HAB / LAB respectively. This is because only one instrument uses the latter, whilst others use the former. This PR:
 

 - Renames HAB / LAB to Front / Rear in the UI
 - Renamed HAB / LAB in the GUI models / presenters. But does not go into the algorithm layer / enums due to size.
 - Fixes a bug introduced in #27895 which prevents us seeing the beam centre values updating (the method went AWOL from the presenter), as it's needed in this PR to validate everything still works
 

 Report to: @smk78 
 

 To test:
 - Download the ISIS Training Data, find the `loqdemo` folder
 - Open ISIS SANS
 - Set the mask file to the `.txt` or `.toml` file in loqdemo
 - Set the batch file to the .csv in the same folder
 - Select the first row, hit load
 - Switch the beam centre finder on the left
 - The rows should be called Front / Rear in the UI. In one drop down there will be `main-detector` and `HAB`, this is expected as it comes from the IDF for LOQ
 - Check the Front / Rear values exist, hit run. After it completes the values in Rear should have updated to the new centre in the text log
 - Change from `main-detector` to `HAB` hit run again. Check the values in front have updated this time.
 

 Part of #30514 
 

 The fix to the beam centre value was introduced this release, so doesn't require release notes

Description of work.
 Create a utility function for direct geometry to return Q_lab, and some angles given HKL, DeltaE, and lattice parameters.


+# Mantid Repository : https://github.com/mantidproject/mantid
+#

+#   NScD Oak Ridge National Laboratory, European Spallation Source,
+#   Institut Laue - Langevin & CSNS, Institute of High Energy Physics, CAS

+from collections import namedtuple
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+import functools
+from typing import Any, Tuple
+import numpy as np
+from mantid.geometry import OrientedLattice
+import mantid.kernel as mk
+from enum import Enum
+import warnings
+warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)
+
+
+__all__ = ['qangle', 'ErrorCodes']
+
+
+def namedtuplefy(func):
+    r"""
+    Decorator to transform the return dictionary of a function into
+    a namedtuple
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    func: Function
+        Function to be decorated
+    name: str
+        Class name for the namedtuple. If None, the name of the function
+        will be used
+    Returns
+    -------
+    Function
+    """
+
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
+        res = func(*args, **kwargs)
+        if wrapper.nt is None:
+            if isinstance(res, Mapping) is False:
+                raise ValueError('Cannot namedtuplefy a non-dict')
+            wrapper.nt = namedtuple(func.__name__ + '_nt', res.keys())
+        return wrapper.nt(**res)
+    wrapper.nt = None
+    return wrapper
+
+
+def _get_angle_from_vectors(x: np.array,
+                            y: np.array,
+                            z: np.array) -> Tuple[np.array, np.array]:
+    """
+    Get the in-plane and out of plane angle from x, y, z vectors
+    Parameters:
+    -----------
+      x, y, z (numpy arrays): x, y, z coordinates of a vector
+    Returns
+    """
+    pass
+
+
+class ErrorCodes(Enum):
+    """
+    Error codes for qangle
+        - 0 correct result
+        - 1 input parameters are wrong for the corresponding hkl
+        - 2 conservation of energy and momentum can't be satisfied
+        - 3 out of plane angle too high
+        - 4 scattering outside detector
+        - 5 scattering in the beam stop
+        - 6 goniometer out of range
+    """
+    CORRECT = 0
+    WRONG_INPUT = 1
+    QE_CONSERVATION = 2
+    OUT_OF_PLANE = 3
+    OUTSIDE_DETECTOR = 4
+    INSIDE_BEAMSTOP = 5
+    GONIOMETR = 6
+
+
+def _qangle_validate_inputs(hkl: np.array,
+                            Ei: float or np.array,
+                            DeltaE: float or np.array,
+                            sign: float or np.array,
+                            lattice: OrientedLattice,
+                            detector_constraints: bool,
+                            horizontal_extent: np.array,
+                            vertical_extent: np.array,
+                            horizontal_extent_low: np.array,
+                            vertical_extent_low: np.array,
+                            goniometer_constraints: bool,
+                            goniometer_range):
+    """
+    Validate inputs for qangle function, according to the rules for
+    that function
+    """
+    try:
+        len_hkl = len(hkl)
+        if len(hkl[0]) != 3:
+            raise ValueError()
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        raise ValueError('hkl is not an array of triplets')
+
+    try:
+        # check if float
+        Ei = float(Ei)
+        Ei = np.full(len_hkl, Ei)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise ValueError('Ei is not a float or numpy array')
+    except TypeError:
+        if len(Ei) != len_hkl:
+            raise ValueError('Ei has different length than hkl')
+    try:
+        # check if float
+        DeltaE = float(DeltaE)
+        DeltaE = np.full(len_hkl, DeltaE)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise ValueError('DeltaE is not a float or numpy array')
+    except TypeError:
+        if len(DeltaE) != len_hkl:
+            raise ValueError('DeltaE has different length than hkl')
+
+    try:
+        # check if int
+        sign = int(sign)
+        sign = np.full(len_hkl,sign)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise ValueError('sign is not an int or numpy array')
+    except TypeError:
+        if len(sign) != len_hkl:
+            raise ValueError('sign has different length than hkl')
+
+    try:
+        UB = lattice.getUB() * 2. * np.pi
+    except:
+        raise ValueError("Can't get the UB matrix from the lattice object")
+
+    # inputs for geometry and goniometer constraints
+    if detector_constraints:
+        if horizontal_extent[0]<-180 or horizontal_extent[1]<horizontal_extent[0] or horizontal_extent[1]>180:
+            raise ValueError("Horizontal constraints must obey -180 <= horizontal_extent[0] <= "
+                             "horizontal_extent[1] <=180")
+        if vertical_extent[0]<-180 or vertical_extent[1]<vertical_extent[0] or vertical_extent[1]>180:
+            raise ValueError("Vertical constraints must obey -180 <= vertical_extent[0] <= "
+                             "vertical_extent[1] <=180")
+        if horizontal_extent_low[0]<-180 or horizontal_extent_low[1]<horizontal_extent_low[0] or horizontal_extent_low[1]>180:
+            raise ValueError("Horizontal constraints must obey -180 <= horizontal_extent_low[0] <= "
+                             "horizontal_extent_low[1] <=180")
+        if vertical_extent_low[0]<-180 or vertical_extent_low[1]<vertical_extent_low[0] or vertical_extent_low[1]>180:
+            raise ValueError("Vertical constraints must obey -180 <= vertical_extent_low[0] <= "
+                             "vertical_extent_low[1] <=180")
+
+    if goniometer_constraints:
+        if goniometer_range[1]<goniometer_range[0] or \
+           goniometer_range[0]<-180. or goniometer_range[1]>180.:
+            raise ValueError("goniometer_range must be an increasing array, "
+                             "with both limits between -180 and 180 degrees")
+
+
+    return (Ei, DeltaE, sign, UB)
+
+
+
+@namedtuplefy
+def qangle(*,  # force keyword arguments
+           Ei: float or np.array,
+           hkl: np.array,  #numpy array of triplets
+           DeltaE: float or np.array,
+           sign: int or np.array,
+           lattice: OrientedLattice,
+           detector_constraints: bool = False,
+           horizontal_extent: np.array = np.array([-180.,180.]),
+           vertical_extent: np.array = np.array([-90.,90.]),
+           horizontal_extent_low: np.array = np.array([0.,0.]),
+           vertical_extent_low: np.array = np.array([0.,0.]),
+           goniometer_constraints: bool = False,
+           goniometer_range: np.array = np.array([-180.,180.]),
+           ) -> namedtuple:
+    """
+    The function calculates the momentum transfer in the lab frame,
+    scattered momentum, and vertical goniometer angle,
+    based on HKL, DeltaE and Ei.
+    Detailed documentation at https://code.ornl.gov/spectroscopy/dgs/status/-/issues/31
+
+    Parameters:
+    -----------
+      Ei (float or numpy array): Incident energy in meV
+      hkl (numpy array of triplets): Reciprocal lattice units for momentum transfer
+      DeltaE (float or numpy array): Energy transfer in meV
+      sign (int or numpy array): Scattering left of the beam (+1) or right (-1)
+      lattice (OrientedLattice): Mantid OrientedLattice object (contains UB matrix)
+      detector_constraints (bool): Flag to consider finite size of detector
+      horizontal_extent (numpy array): Horizontal angle extent of the detector in degrees (-180 to 180)
+      vertical_extent (numpy array): Vertical angle extent of the detector in degrees (-90 to 90)
+      horizontal_extent_low (numpy array): Horizontal angle extent of the beam stop in degrees (-180 to 180)
+      vertical_extent_low (numpy array): Vertical angle extent of the beam stop in degrees
+      goniometer constraints (bool): Flag to restrict the range of the goniometer
+      goniometer_range (numpy array): Goniometer angle range in degrees (in the -180 to 180 range)
+
+    Retuns:
+    -------
+      (namedtuple): namedtuple containing
+        - Q_lab_x, Q_lab_y, Q_lab_z (numpy arrays): Q in the lab frame
+        - in_plane_Q_angle, out_plane_Q_angle (numpy arrays): in plane and out of plane angles for Q_lab
+        - in_plane_kf_angle, out_plane_kf_angle (numpy arrays): in plane and out of plane angles for scattered beam
+        - goniometer (numpy array): goniometer angle in degrees (-180 to 180)
+        - error code (numpy array): error codes
+
+    Raises:
+    -------
+      ValueError if input parameters are not as described above
+
+    Notes:
+    -----
+    1. Where the error code is not 0, the corresponding entries in the other vector might be set to NaN
+    2. If detector_constraints is False, entries for horizontal_extent, vertical_extent,
+    horizontal_extent_low, vertical_extent_low are ignored
+    3. If goniometer_constraints is False, goniometer_range is ignored
+    """
+    # Note for developers: formulas from
+    # https://github.com/mantidproject/documents/blob/master/Design/UBMatriximplementationnotes.pdf
+
+    # check input parameters
+    Ei, DeltaE, sign, UB = _qangle_validate_inputs(hkl, Ei, DeltaE, sign, lattice, detector_constraints,
+                                                   horizontal_extent, vertical_extent, horizontal_extent_low,
+                                                   vertical_extent_low, goniometer_constraints, goniometer_range)
+
+    error_code = np.full((len(hkl)), ErrorCodes.CORRECT)
+
+    # conversion factor from momentum (inverse Angstroms) to energy (meV) - E = E2k * k**2
+    E2k = mk.PhysicalConstants.E_mev_toNeutronWavenumberSq
+
+    # Q_sample =2Pi(hkl) (the multiplication with 2pi was done in validation) (eq 5-7)
+    Q_sample_x, Q_sample_y, Q_sample_z = np.matmul(UB, hkl.T)
+    k_i = np.sqrt(Ei/E2k)
+    k_f = np.sqrt((Ei-DeltaE)/E2k)
+
+    # if any of the above elements in the array is NaN or inf, you get error_code 1 (or 2 if only kf is wrong)
+    error_code[np.logical_not(np.isfinite(k_f))] = ErrorCodes.QE_CONSERVATION
+    error_code[np.logical_not(np.isfinite(Q_sample_x + Q_sample_y + Q_sample_z + k_i))] = ErrorCodes.WRONG_INPUT
+
+    # calculate delta (eq 121)
+    error_code[np.abs(Q_sample_y) > 0.9998 * k_f] = ErrorCodes.OUT_OF_PLANE
+    delta = -np.arcsin(Q_sample_y / k_f)
+
+    # calculate chi (eq 125)
+    chi = np.arccos((k_i**2 + k_f**2 - Q_sample_x**2 - Q_sample_y**2 - Q_sample_z**2)/(2 * k_i * k_f *np.cos(delta)))
+    bad_chi = np.logical_not(np.isfinite(chi))
+    error_code[np.logical_and(bad_chi, error_code == ErrorCodes.CORRECT)] = ErrorCodes.QE_CONSERVATION
+
+    # check left/right
+    bad_sign = np.abs(sign)!=1
+    chi *= sign
+    chi[bad_sign] = np.nan
+    delta[bad_sign] = np.nan
+    error_code[bad_sign] = ErrorCodes.WRONG_INPUT
+
+    # calculate Q_lab (eq 118)
+    Q_lab_x = -k_f * np.cos(delta) * np.sin(chi)
+    Q_lab_y = Q_sample_y
+    Q_lab_z = k_i - k_f * np.cos(delta) * np.cos(chi)
+
+    # calculate angles Q_lab
+    in_plane_Q_angle = np.arctan2(Q_lab_x, Q_lab_z)
+    out_plane_Q_angle = np.arcsin(Q_lab_y/np.sqrt(Q_lab_x**2 + Q_lab_y**2 + Q_lab_z**2))
+
+    # calculate omega (eq 126)
+    omega = np.arctan2(Q_lab_x, Q_lab_z) - np.arctan2(Q_sample_x, Q_sample_z)
+    omega[omega>np.pi] -= 2*np.pi
+    omega[omega<-np.pi] += 2*np.pi
+
+    # transform all angles to degrees
+    chi = np.degrees(chi)
+    delta = np.degrees(delta)
+    omega = np.degrees(omega)
+    in_plane_Q_angle = np.degrees(in_plane_Q_angle)
+    out_plane_Q_angle = np.degrees(out_plane_Q_angle)
+
+    if detector_constraints:
+        error_code[((chi<horizontal_extent[0]) | (chi>horizontal_extent[1]) |
+                   (delta<vertical_extent[0]) | (delta>vertical_extent[1]))
+                   & (error_code==ErrorCodes.CORRECT)
+                    ] =  ErrorCodes.OUTSIDE_DETECTOR
+        error_code[(chi>horizontal_extent_low[0]) & (chi<horizontal_extent_low[1]) &
+                   (delta>vertical_extent_low[0]) & (delta<vertical_extent_low[1]) & (error_code==ErrorCodes.CORRECT)
+                   ] =  ErrorCodes.INSIDE_BEAMSTOP

title: Ornl direct utils
body:
Description of work.
 Create a utility function for direct geometry to return Q_lab, and some angles given HKL, DeltaE, and lattice parameters.
 

 To test:
 

 <!-- Instructions for testing. -->
 ```python
 import numpy as np
 from mantid.utils.dgs import qangle, ErrorCodes
 from mantid.geometry import OrientedLattice
 

 a=3
 b=7
 c=10
 alpha=90
 beta=90
 gamma=120
 u=[1,0,0]
 v=[0,1,0]
 ol=OrientedLattice(a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma)
 ol.setUFromVectors(u,v)
 

 result = qangle(lattice=ol,Ei=10,DeltaE=0, hkl=np.array([[1,0,0]]), sign=1)
 print(result)
 print(result.error_code[0]==ErrorCodes.CORRECT)
 ```
 

 *There is no associated issue in Mantid repo.* The ORNL issue is https://code.ornl.gov/spectroscopy/dgs/status/-/issues/31

 Finally, don't forget to add the appropriate labels, milestones, etc.! -->

+def namedtuplefy(func):
+    r"""
+    Decorator to transform the return dictionary of a function into
+    a namedtuple
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    func: Function
+        Function to be decorated
+    name: str
+        Class name for the namedtuple. If None, the name of the function
+        will be used
+    Returns

+    Function
+    """

+                raise ValueError('Cannot namedtuplefy a non-dict')

+@namedtuplefy
+def qangle(*,  # force keyword arguments
+           Ei: float or np.array,
+           hkl: np.array,  #numpy array of triplets
+           DeltaE: float or np.array,
+           sign: int or np.array,
+           lattice: OrientedLattice,
+           detector_constraints: bool = False,
+           horizontal_extent: np.array = np.array([-180.,180.]),
+           vertical_extent: np.array = np.array([-90.,90.]),
+           horizontal_extent_low: np.array = np.array([0.,0.]),
+           vertical_extent_low: np.array = np.array([0.,0.]),
+           goniometer_constraints: bool = False,
+           goniometer_range: np.array = np.array([-180.,180.]),
+           ) -> namedtuple:
+    """
+    The function calculates the momentum transfer in the lab frame,
+    scattered momentum, and vertical goniometer angle,
+    based on HKL, DeltaE and Ei.
+    Detailed documentation at https://code.ornl.gov/spectroscopy/dgs/status/-/issues/31
+
+    Parameters:
+    -----------
+      Ei (float or numpy array): Incident energy in meV
+      hkl (numpy array of triplets): Reciprocal lattice units for momentum transfer
+      DeltaE (float or numpy array): Energy transfer in meV
+      sign (int or numpy array): Scattering left of the beam (+1) or right (-1)
+      lattice (OrientedLattice): Mantid OrientedLattice object (contains UB matrix)
+      detector_constraints (bool): Flag to consider finite size of detector
+      horizontal_extent (numpy array): Horizontal angle extent of the detector in degrees (-180 to 180)
+      vertical_extent (numpy array): Vertical angle extent of the detector in degrees (-90 to 90)
+      horizontal_extent_low (numpy array): Horizontal angle extent of the beam stop in degrees (-180 to 180)
+      vertical_extent_low (numpy array): Vertical angle extent of the beam stop in degrees
+      goniometer constraints (bool): Flag to restrict the range of the goniometer
+      goniometer_range (numpy array): Goniometer angle range in degrees (in the -180 to 180 range)
+
+    Retuns:
+    -------
+      (namedtuple): namedtuple containing
+        - Q_lab_x, Q_lab_y, Q_lab_z (numpy arrays): Q in the lab frame
+        - in_plane_Q_angle, out_plane_Q_angle (numpy arrays): in plane and out of plane angles for Q_lab
+        - in_plane_kf_angle, out_plane_kf_angle (numpy arrays): in plane and out of plane angles for scattered beam
+        - goniometer (numpy array): goniometer angle in degrees (-180 to 180)
+        - error code (numpy array): error codes
+
+    Raises:
+    -------
+      ValueError if input parameters are not as described above
+
+    Notes:
+    -----
+    1. Where the error code is not 0, the corresponding entries in the other vector might be set to NaN
+    2. If detector_constraints is False, entries for horizontal_extent, vertical_extent,
+    horizontal_extent_low, vertical_extent_low are ignored
+    3. If goniometer_constraints is False, goniometer_range is ignored
+    """
+    # Note for developers: formulas from
+    # https://github.com/mantidproject/documents/blob/master/Design/UBMatriximplementationnotes.pdf
+
+    # check input parameters
+    Ei, DeltaE, sign, UB = _qangle_validate_inputs(hkl, Ei, DeltaE, sign, lattice, detector_constraints,
+                                                   horizontal_extent, vertical_extent, horizontal_extent_low,
+                                                   vertical_extent_low, goniometer_constraints, goniometer_range)
+
+    error_code = np.full((len(hkl)), ErrorCodes.CORRECT)
+
+    # conversion factor from momentum (inverse Angstroms) to energy (meV) - E = E2k * k**2
+    E2k = mk.PhysicalConstants.E_mev_toNeutronWavenumberSq
+
+    # Q_sample =2Pi(hkl) (the multiplication with 2pi was done in validation) (eq 5-7)
+    Q_sample_x, Q_sample_y, Q_sample_z = np.matmul(UB, hkl.T)
+    k_i = np.sqrt(Ei/E2k)
+    k_f = np.sqrt((Ei-DeltaE)/E2k)
+
+    # if any of the above elements in the array is NaN or inf, you get error_code 1 (or 2 if only kf is wrong)
+    error_code[np.logical_not(np.isfinite(k_f))] = ErrorCodes.QE_CONSERVATION
+    error_code[np.logical_not(np.isfinite(Q_sample_x + Q_sample_y + Q_sample_z + k_i))] = ErrorCodes.WRONG_INPUT
+
+    # calculate delta (eq 121)
+    error_code[np.abs(Q_sample_y) > 0.9998 * k_f] = ErrorCodes.OUT_OF_PLANE
+    delta = -np.arcsin(Q_sample_y / k_f)
+
+    # calculate chi (eq 125)
+    chi = np.arccos((k_i**2 + k_f**2 - Q_sample_x**2 - Q_sample_y**2 - Q_sample_z**2)/(2 * k_i * k_f *np.cos(delta)))
+    bad_chi = np.logical_not(np.isfinite(chi))
+    error_code[np.logical_and(bad_chi, error_code == ErrorCodes.CORRECT)] = ErrorCodes.QE_CONSERVATION
+
+    # check left/right
+    bad_sign = np.abs(sign)!=1
+    chi *= sign
+    chi[bad_sign] = np.nan
+    delta[bad_sign] = np.nan
+    error_code[bad_sign] = ErrorCodes.WRONG_INPUT
+
+    # calculate Q_lab (eq 118)
+    Q_lab_x = -k_f * np.cos(delta) * np.sin(chi)
+    Q_lab_y = Q_sample_y
+    Q_lab_z = k_i - k_f * np.cos(delta) * np.cos(chi)
+
+    # calculate angles Q_lab
+    in_plane_Q_angle = np.arctan2(Q_lab_x, Q_lab_z)
+    out_plane_Q_angle = np.arcsin(Q_lab_y/np.sqrt(Q_lab_x**2 + Q_lab_y**2 + Q_lab_z**2))
+
+    # calculate omega (eq 126)
+    omega = np.arctan2(Q_lab_x, Q_lab_z) - np.arctan2(Q_sample_x, Q_sample_z)
+    omega[omega>np.pi] -= 2*np.pi
+    omega[omega<-np.pi] += 2*np.pi
+
+    # transform all angles to degrees
+    chi = np.degrees(chi)
+    delta = np.degrees(delta)
+    omega = np.degrees(omega)
+    in_plane_Q_angle = np.degrees(in_plane_Q_angle)
+    out_plane_Q_angle = np.degrees(out_plane_Q_angle)
+
+    if detector_constraints:
+        error_code[((chi<horizontal_extent[0]) | (chi>horizontal_extent[1]) |
+                   (delta<vertical_extent[0]) | (delta>vertical_extent[1]))
+                   & (error_code==ErrorCodes.CORRECT)
+                    ] =  ErrorCodes.OUTSIDE_DETECTOR
+        error_code[(chi>horizontal_extent_low[0]) & (chi<horizontal_extent_low[1]) &
+                   (delta>vertical_extent_low[0]) & (delta<vertical_extent_low[1]) & (error_code==ErrorCodes.CORRECT)
+                   ] =  ErrorCodes.INSIDE_BEAMSTOP
+
+    if goniometer_constraints:
+        error_code[((omega< goniometer_range[0]) | (omega> goniometer_range[1])) & (error_code==ErrorCodes.CORRECT)
+        ] = ErrorCodes.GONIOMETR
+
+    return dict(Q_lab_x=Q_lab_x, Q_lab_y=Q_lab_y, Q_lab_z=Q_lab_z,
+                in_plane_Q_angle = in_plane_Q_angle, out_plane_Q_angle = out_plane_Q_angle,
+                in_plane_kf_angle = chi, out_plane_kf_angle = delta,
+                omega=omega, error_code=error_code)
+

title: SaveCanSAS and SaveAscii2 - one spectrum per file
body:
Description of work.
 

 This PR introduces a new boolean parameter for the SaveCanSAS algorithm: `OneSpectrumPerFile`.
 * if `true`, the algorithm will produce one file per spectrum
 * if `false` all spectra will be added to the same file in separate `<SASdata>` entries.
 

 This seems to correspond to the CanSAS file specifications: http://www.cansas.org/formats/canSAS1d/1.1/doc/overview.html#xml-layout-for-multiple-experiments
 

 To test:
 

 * Create a sample workspace
 ```python
 from mantid.simpleapi import *
 CreateSampleWorkspace(OutputWorkspace="ws")
 ```
 * Export with SaveCanSAS, use the OneSpectrumPerFile option to modify the behavior.
 * Observe the files and try to open them with SASView or any program that is able to read cansas files (concerning SASView, the current release is not able to properly load file with multiple `<SASdata>`, the code containing this PR should be used instead: https://github.com/SasView/sasview/pull/1890)

This PR adds support to reduce single-crystal data measured by D7 instrument at the ILL in `PolDiffILLReduction` and `D7AbsoluteCrossSections` algorithms.
 

 - [x] Optimise the processing time of 400+ files of an omega-scan. Achieved with replacing `Load` with `LoadAndMerge` and conjoining workspaces provided by `PolDiffILLReduction` into 2D workspaces containing the entire omega scan. 
 - [x] Add anisotropic magnetism cross-section separation based on _W. Schweika 2010 J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 211 012026_.
 - [x] Output the single crystal reduced data as a mapped on a Qx - Qy plane, reimplementingLAMP's QRebin method.
 - [x] Verify that the separated cross-sections are comparable with results from LAMP.
 

 Recalculation of X and Y axes values can be done outside of the reduction and normalisation algorithms, for example as a part of the reduction script.

+.. _muon_corrections_tab-ref:
+
+Corrections Tab
+---------------
+
+.. image::  ../../images/muon_interface_tab_corrections.png
+   :align: right
+   :height: 400px
+
+The corrections tab is used for correcting the data to be analysed.
+There are two types of corrections; dead time corrections, and background corrections.
+
+**Runs** Allows you to select the runs to display correction data for.
+
+Dead Time Corrections
+^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
+
+**Dead Time for all runs** This allows you to select the method to use for dead time corrections for all runs. There are four deadtime correction options:
+
+* ``From data file``: The deadtime table will be taken from the relevant data file
+* ``From table workspace``: A previously loaded deadtime table may be selected which will then be used in all group and pair calculations.
+* ``From other file``: A file may be selected to load a deadtime table from this will then be used in all group and pair calculations.
+* ``None``: No deadtime corrections should be applied.
+
+**Dead Time stats** Displays the minimum, maximum and average deadtime correction for the currently selected runs.
+
+Background Corrections
+^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
+
+**Background** There are three background correction options:
+
+* ``None``: No background correction should be applied.
+* ``Auto``: The background is automatically calculated by performing a fit on the loaded data before being subtracted from the data. The accompanying diagram describes this process.
+* ``Manual``: The background is entered manually by the user before being subtracted from the data.
+
+.. image::  ../../images/muon_auto_corrections_flowchart.PNG
+   :align: right
+   :height: 400px
+
+**Select Function** This is only available when in ``Auto`` mode. It allows you to choose between using a ``Flat Background + Exp Decay``, or just a ``Flat Background`` to calculate the background. The Lambda value in the Exp Decay is fixed to a value of 1.0 over the muon lifetime.
+
+**Show data for** There are two options for selecting which data should be displayed:
+
+* ``All Runs``: Displays the correction data for all loaded runs when ticked. If it isn't ticked, only correction data for the currently selected runs are shown.
+* ``Select Group``: Displays the correction data for all groups, or a specific group.
+
+**Apply parameter changes to all domains** Changes made in the corrections data table will be applied to all domains when this option is ticked.
+
+The corrections data table contains the data used for the background subtractions of each domain:
+
+**Run** The run number corresponding to a specific domain.
+
+**Group** The group corresponding to a specific domain.
+
+**Use Raw** This is only available when in ``Auto`` mode, and the fixed rebin option is selected. It is used to specify whether the raw or rebinned data is used to calculate the background.
+
+**Start X** This is only available when in ``Auto`` mode. It is the Start X used for the fit to calculate the background.
+
+**End X** This is only available when in ``Auto`` mode. It is the End X used for the fit to calculate the background.
+
+**BG** The background that has been calculated and subtracted from the corresponding data.
+
+**BG Error** This is only available when in ``Auto`` mode. It is the error in the calculated background.
+
+**Status** This states whether or not the correction was successful for a domain. A correction will be skipped if the chi squared of a fit is greater than 10.
+
+**Fit Output** This is only available when in ``Auto`` mode. The button will open the parameters table and normalised covariance matrix for the performed background fit.
+
+Used By
+^^^^^^^
+
+:ref:`Muon Analysis <Muon_Analysis-ref>`,
+:ref:`Frequency Domain Analysis <Frequency_Domain_Analysis-ref>`

title: Port ISIS Sans to use Qt adaptor
body:
Description of work.
 

  Switch SANS Components to Qt/Threading adaptor
  
  Switches all the SANS components away from a bespoke threading solution
  to the generic Qt Threading adaptor.
  
  This brings a number of advantages:
  - Stack traces without execute() steps included
  - Increased responsiveness (subjectively)
  - Better tooling support
 

 Note The methods in files belonging to the `_async` module were cut and paste from the existing models / presenters (where they incorrectly resided.
 As this is a cut and paste a reviewer is welcome to review each method, but does not need to for new async files.

title: Frequency Domain Analysis - Dataset filter for sequential fitting
body:
Description of work.
 This PR allows the filtering of datasets in the Sequential Fitting tab of FDA so that the imaginary, real, modulus or maxent domains can be selected before doing a sequential fit.
 

 To test:
 1. Open Frequency Domain Analysis
 2. Load MUSR62260-1
 3. Go to the Transform tab
 4. Calculate FFT for `MUSR62260; Group; fwd; Asymmetry; FD` and `MUSR62261; Group; fwd; Asymmetry; FD`
 5. Calculate MaxEnt for `MUSR62260_raw_data FD` and `MUSR62261_raw_data FD` 
 6. Go to the Fitting tab and add a function
 7. Go to the Sequential Fitting tab
 8. Switch between `All`, `FD_Re`, `FD_Im`, `FD_mod` and `MaxEnt`. Try sequential fitting for each and make sure the relevant dataset names are displayed in the table.
 9. Go to Muon Analysis and check that this combo box is hidden, and that `All` datasets are displayed at all times.

title: New algorithm to refine lattice parameters across runs with separate U matrix/orientation
body:
Description of work.
 

 New algorithm `FindGlobalBMatrix` to refine the lattice parameters (encoded in the B matrix) across many runs with separate U matrix/orientation which is useful for when the goniometer is inaccurate/not well known.
 

 The quantity minimised is the average of the square of the difference in `QSample` between peak the peak at integer HKL (the minimisation is performed by scipy `leastsq` function). The average rather than the sum of the squared residuals is used so as not to penalise the indexing of more peaks as the UB matrix becomes more accurate.

+.. algorithm::
+
+.. summary::
+
+.. relatedalgorithms::
+
+.. properties::
+
+Description
+-----------
+
+FindGlobalBMatrix refines the lattice parameters (encoded in the B matrix) across PeaksWorkspaces from multiple runs
+with a separate U matrix (which encodes the orientation for an identity goniometer matrix) per run. This is useful for
+when the goniometer matrix is inaccurate/not well known.
+
+The quantity minimised is the average of the square of the difference in QSample between the observed peak and the peak
+at integer HKL (see :ref:`algm-CalculateUMatrix` for details). The average rather than the sum of the squared residuals
+is used so as not to penalise the indexing of more peaks as the UB matrix becomes more accurate.
+
+FindGlobalBMatrix adds a different UB to each peak workspace that can be indexed - note the algorithm ensures consistent
+indexing across all runs (i.e. axes are not swapped or inverted). All peaks workspaces must have more then 6 peaks in
+(a requirement of some child algorithms used).
+
+The algorithm proceeds in this way:
+
+-  Finds an initial UB
+
+   -  If a UB exists on any workspace the initial is the UB that indexes the most peaks.
+   -  Otherwise :ref:`FindUBUsingLatticeParameters<algm-FindUBUsingLatticeParameters>` is run on the workspaces with the input lattice parameters until a UB is found.
+
+-  Peaks in all workspaces are indexed consistently with the initial UB
+
+   -  If a workspace has a valid UB it is transformed to preserve consistent indexing.
+   -  Otherwise we try to index the peaks using the initial UB and the goniometer matrix on the workspace
+   -  If the above doesn't work because e.g. the goniometer matrix is inaccurate, we find a UB using :ref:`FindUBUsingLatticeParameters<algm-FindUBUsingLatticeParameters>` and transform to preserve consistent indexing.
+
+-  Once peaks are indexed the optimal lattice parameters are found that minimise the average of the squared residuals in QSample across all runs.
+
+   -  The U matrix of each run is found for a given set of lattice parameters using :ref:`algm-CalculateUMatrix`.
+
+
+Useage
+-----------
+
+**Example:**
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+
+    from mantid.simpleapi import *
+
+    # load empty instrument so can create a peak table
+    ws = LoadEmptyInstrument(InstrumentName='SXD', OutputWorkspace='empty_SXD')
+    axis = ws.getAxis(0)
+    axis.setUnit("TOF")
+
+    # create two peak tables with UB corresponding to different lattice constants, a
+    peaks1 = CreatePeaksWorkspace(InstrumentWorkspace=ws, NumberOfPeaks=0)
+    UB = np.diag([1.0/3.8, 0.25, 0.1])  # alatt = [3.8, 4, 10]
+    SetUB(peaks1, UB=UB)
+    peaks2 = CreatePeaksWorkspace(InstrumentWorkspace=ws, NumberOfPeaks=0)
+    UB = np.diag([1.0/4.2, 0.25, 0.1])  # alatt = [4.2, 4, 10]
+    SetUB(peaks2, UB=UB)
+    # Add some peaks
+    for h in range(0, 3):
+        for k in range(0, 3):
+            for peaks in [peaks1, peaks2]:
+                pk = peaks.createPeakHKL([h, k, 4])
+                peaks.addPeak(pk)
+
+    FindGlobalBMatrix(PeakWorkspaces=[peaks1, peaks2], a=4.1, b=4.2, c=10, alpha=88, beta=88, gamma=89,
+                      Tolerance=0.15)
+
+    # show that both workspaces have the average of the two a lattice constants (a=4 Ang)
+    print(peaks1.sample().getOrientedLattice())
+    # lattice parameters: a = 4.00025 b = 3.98794 c = 9.99608 alpha = 89.9698 beta = 90.0829 gamma = 89.9336
+
+    print(peaks2.sample().getOrientedLattice())
+    # lattice parameters: a = 4.00025 b = 3.98794 c = 9.99608 alpha = 89.9698 beta = 90.0829 gamma = 89.9336
+

title: Fit Script Generator - Output Base Name and Plot Output options
body:
Description of work.
 This PR adds two options to the Fit Script Generator to be used when generating a python script:
 

 - `Output Base Name` allows you to specify a different base name for your output fit workspaces
 - `Plot Output` allows you to turn off/on the plotting of the output fit workspaces.
 

 The PR also renames the `BasicFitOptionsBrowser` to be the `FitScriptOptionsBrowser` because it now contains an option specific to the fit script that you generate.
 

 To test:
 1. Comment out this line
 https://github.com/mantidproject/mantid/blob/5077722a251590b9196563d8d23245ce15e04699/scripts/Muon/GUI/Common/fitting_widgets/basic_fitting/fit_controls_view.py#L28
 1. Open Muon Analysis interface
 2. Load MUSR 62260
 3. Go to Fitting tab and click `Fit Generator`
 4. When the `Fit Script Generator` opens, there should be 4 domains loaded into the interface
 5. Add a `GausOsc` function to all domains
 6. Change the `Output Base Name` (bottom right)

title: Add Bk2BkExpConvPV parameters for ENGINX and improve FWHM of function
body:
Description of work.
 

 - Add parameters for `Bk2BkExpConvPV` for ENGINX.
 - Fix bug in pseud-voigt FWHM, `H`, and the mixing parameter `eta` - it should use the FWHM of Lorz (`2*gamma`) [1]
 - Add setter for FWHM using Eq. in `BackToBackExponential` (which only has Gaussian component). Assuming the Voigt has same FWHM as Gaussian in `BackToBAckExponential` then solving Eq. for `H` assuming `H_L = H_G` (i.e. Gaussian and Lorz components of voigt have same FWHM).
 

 [1] P. Thompson, D. E. Cox and J. B. Hastings (1987). "Rietveld refinement of Debye-Scherrer synchrotron X-ray data from Al2O3". Journal of Applied Crystallography. 20 (2): 7983. doi:10.1107/S0021889887087090.

body:
Description of work.
 In sequential fitting in Muon Analysis GUI it is now possible to set the fit parameters for one run and copy it to all the other runs. The changes are kept if you switch to TF Symmetry mode.

 7. Change the value of A on line 5 to a value of your choice. The value of A in each line of the table should change to your new value.
 8. Untick the checkbox ```Copy fit parameters to all```
 9. Change the value of A in any row to a value of your choice. Only that cell should change, the rest of the column should retain the value you updated to in step 7.

title: D7 Powder reduction user feedback
body:
This PR implements D7 users feedback to the current state of the powder reduction algorithms: PolDiffILLReduction and D7AbsoluteCrossSections. These could be summarised as:
 

 

 - [x] The order of polarisation orientation in the data is not always spin-flip->non-spin-flip as assumed in the reduction chain, leading to incorrect polarisation correction values and separated cross-sections when this is not the case.
 - [x] Reduction of verbosity of input parameters: 'input' could be dropped from 'CadmiumInputWorkspace', 'EmptyInputWorkspace', etc.
 - [x] Specifying '_1' as part of the name for certain input workspaces is tedious and when not used can lead to confusing error messages : fixed by changing the type of input workspaces to `WorkspaceGroup`.
 - [x] Change the sample density from number to mass density
 - [x] Add simple self-attenuation approximation by scaling the reduced data by transmission value
 ~~Add 'measured' attenuation approximate method for self-attenuation correction~~ This will be implemented at a later stage
 - [x] Formula units parameter is redundant, it is always equal to unity
 - [x] Multiple empty beam measurements are possible, and they should be properly normalised when there is more than one input, which especially relevant for transmission calculation
 - [x] Add option to normalise either by monitor or time (duration)
 - [x] Comments between lines in the documentation can be confusing, especially about cadmium transmission
 - [x] Change the default naming scheme of workspaces in group when loading files from counting '_1', '_2' to one containing relevant information about polarisation, e.g. '*_Z_ON'
 - [x] Validate whether averaging of the measured intensities before processing (e.g. polarisation correction) produces consistent outcome with averaging after processing, check for possible performance boost; this is already done, other workflows would collide with applying corrections correctly
 - [x] Y unit for vanadium output from PolDIffILLReduction is incorrect
 - [x] Diagnostics: An option for quartz and vanadium data be averaged according to detector/bank TwoTheta. Currently implemented averaging per polarisation orientation is not sufficient.
 - [x] Diagnostics: An option to display all measured sample data on a single scatter plot.

title: IntegrateEllipsoid now use separate integrators for Bragg peaks and satellite peaks
body:
Description of work.
 

 <!-- If the original issue was raised by a user they should be named here. Do not leak email addresses
 Report to: [user name]
 -->
 

 - Original Gitlab user story: [SCD369](https://code.ornl.gov/sns-hfir-scse/diffraction/single-crystal/single-crystal-diffraction/-/issues/369)
 - This is #32008 into `master`
 

 The original `IntegrateEllipsoid` uses a single integrator to process all peaks in given workspace, which forced the users to
 

 - separate Bragg peaks and satellite peaks prior to integration
 - run integration for the two set of peaks independently
 - merge the results back into a single workspace
 

 This PR introduces one additional integrator (for satellite peaks) such that
 

 - if no satellite peak options are specified -> treat satellite peaks the same as Bragg peaks
 - else -> use `integrator_satellite` to integrate satellite peaks while using `integrator` for regular Bragg peaks.
 

 This new feature help simplify the workflow on the user end.

title: Create mesh for CSGObject to plot Sample Shapes
body:
Description of work.
 

 A mesh can now be created for CSGObjects to plot Sample Shapes, such as spheres + cylinders and shapes can be merged.
 

 Refs #30607 
 

 To test:
 

 - Run the script below
 - Edit `SetSample(...)` to use the xml strings in the script for different shapes, and check that sphere, cylinder and a sphere with a cylindrical hole in work!
 - Feel free to try some weird and wonderful shapes and combinations of shapes: https://docs.mantidproject.org/nightly/concepts/HowToDefineGeometricShape.html#howtodefinegeometricshape
 

 

 ```
 # import mantid algorithms, numpy and matplotlib
 from mantid.simpleapi import *
 import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
 import numpy as np
 from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.art3d import Poly3DCollection
 from mantid.api import AnalysisDataService as ADS
 

 

 # A fake host workspace, replace this with your real one.
 ws = CreateSampleWorkspace()
 

 cuboid_xml = " \
 <cuboid id='some-cuboid'> \
  <height val='20.0' /> \
  <width val='50.0' /> \
  <depth val='20.0' /> \
  <centre x='100.0' y='100.0' z='100.0' /> \
  <rotation x='60' y='90' z='217' /> \
 </cuboid> \
 <algebra val='some-cuboid' /> \
 "
 

 sphere_xml = " \
 <sphere id='some-sphere'> \
  <centre x='0.0' y='0.0' z='0.0' /> \
  <radius val='0.5' /> \
 </sphere> \
 <algebra val='some-sphere' /> \
 "
 

 cylinder_xml = " \
 <cylinder id='some-cylinder'> \
  <centre-of-bottom-base r='0.0' t='0.0' p='0.0' /> \
  <axis x='0.0' y='0.2' z='0' /> \
  <radius val='1' /> \
  <height val='10.2' /> \
 </cylinder> \
 <algebra val='some-cylinder' /> \
 "
 

 merge_xml = ' \
 <cylinder id="stick"> \
  <centre-of-bottom-base x="-0.5" y="0.0" z="0.0" /> \
  <axis x="1.0" y="0.0" z="0.0" /> \
  <radius val="0.2" /> \
  <height val="1.0" /> \
 </cylinder> \
 \
 <sphere id="some-sphere"> \
  <centre x="0.0" y="0.0" z="0.0" /> \
  <radius val="0.5" /> \
 </sphere> \
 \
 <algebra val="some-sphere (#stick)" /> \
 '
 

 flat_circle = " \
 <cylinder id=\"pixel-shape\"> \
  <centre-of-bottom-base x=\"0\" y=\"-0.0001\" z=\"0\"/> \
  <axis x=\"0\" y=\"1\" z=\"0\"/><radius val=\"0.004\"/> \
  <height val=\"0.0002\"/> \
 </cylinder>"
 

 # Set sample geometry of workspace to this CSG object
 SetSample(ws, Geometry={'Shape': 'CSG', 'Value': cuboid_xml})
 

 sample = ws.sample()
 shape = sample.getShape()
 mesh = shape.getMesh()
 

 facecolors = ['royalblue','b','red','firebrick', 'gold', 'orange','green', 'darkgreen','grey','black', 'purple', 'mediumorchid']
 

 mesh_polygon_a = Poly3DCollection(mesh, facecolors = facecolors, edgecolors='green', linewidths=0.1, alpha = 0.5)
 '''Problem based on order of being added!'''
 

 fig, axes = plt.subplots(subplot_kw={'projection':'mantid3d'})
 axes.add_collection3d(mesh_polygon_a)
 

 # Auto scale to the mesh size
 axes_lims = mesh.flatten()
 axes.auto_scale_xyz(axes_lims, axes_lims, axes_lims)
 

 axes.set_title('Sample Shape: Cuboid')
 axes.set_xlabel('X / m')
 axes.set_ylabel('Y / m')
 axes.set_zlabel('Z / m')
 

 plt.show()
 ```

title: TOF Powder group calibration scripts
body:
Description of work.
 

 Workflow for [PD240](https://code.ornl.gov/sns-hfir-scse/diffraction/powder/powder-diffraction/-/issues/240)
 

 

 To test:
 

 The usage example should be a good test to run through.
 

 Here is a real example, just loading a few banks and creating groups by bank
 

 ```python
 from mantid.simpleapi import *
 from Calibration.tofpd import group_calibration
 

 data_file = 'NOM_144974'
 

 data = LoadEventNexus(data_file, BankName='bank45,bank46,bank47,bank48,bank49', NumberOfBins=1)
 data = MaskDetectorsIf(data, Operator='Less', Value=25000)
 

 groups, _, _ = CreateGroupingWorkspace(data, GroupDetectorsBy='bank', OutputWorkspace='group_banks')
 

 output_workspace_basename = 'calibration'
 

 cc_diffcal = group_calibration.cc_calibrate_groups(data,
  groups,
  output_workspace_basename)
 

 # Check CC calibration
 data_d = ConvertUnits(data, Target='dSpacing')
 data_d = Rebin(data_d, '0.25,0.002,2.25')
 data_aligned = AlignDetectors(data, CalibrationWorkspace=cc_diffcal)
 data_aligned = Rebin(data_aligned, '0.25,0.002,2.25')
 

 diffcal, mask = group_calibration.pdcalibration_groups(data,
  groups,
  cc_diffcal,
  output_workspace_basename,
  PeakWindow=0.4)
 

 # Check final calibration
 data_aligned2 = AlignDetectors(data, CalibrationWorkspace=diffcal)
 data_aligned2 = Rebin(data_aligned2, '0.25,0.002,2.25')
 ```
 

 You can look at the starting `data_d` workspace and compare to after CC `data_aligned` and after CC+PD `data_aligned2`. The Colorfill plot is good to look at.

+
+.. _calibration_tofpd_group_calibration-ref:
+
+Group Calibration
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+Some script have been created that provided a workflow for calibrating
+the instrument in groups using a combination of :ref:`CrossCorrelate
+<algm-CrossCorrelate>`, :ref:`GetDetectorOffsets
+<algm-GetDetectorOffsets>` and :ref:`PDCalibration
+<algm-PDCalibration>`.
+
+It works by performing the cross-correlations on only the detectors
+within a group, after which the grouped detectors are merge together
+to use with PDCalibration. The difc from the PDCalibration and
+cross-correlation are combined using :ref:`CombineDiffCal
+<algm-CombineDiffCal>`
+
+The workflow follows these step:
+
+#. Load data, usually diamond
+#. Convert to d-spacing
+#. CrossCorrelate a portion of the instrument according to the group information
+#. GetDetectorOffsets to calculate offsets for individual pixels with a group
+#. ConvertDiffCal to convert these constants to :math:`DIFC_{CC}`
+#. Use :math:`DIFC_{CC}` to convert the origonal data to d-spacing. DiffractionFocus allows for combining a portion of the instrument into a single spectrum for improved statistics
+#. Pick an arbitrary constant, :math:`DIFC_{arb}` to convert this combined spectrum back to time-of-flight
+#. PDCalibration the combined spectrum to determine a conversion constant :math:`DIFC_{PD}`
+#. Use :ref:`CombineDiffCal <algm-CombineDiffCal>` to combine :math:`DIFC_{CC}`, :math:`DIFC_{arb}`, and :math:`DIFC_{PD}` into a new calibration constant, :math:`DIFC_{eff}`
+
+.. testcode:: group_cal
+
+    # create a fake starting workspace in d-spacing then convert to TOF for calibration
+    myFunc = "name=Gaussian, PeakCentre=1, Height=100, Sigma=0.01;name=Gaussian, PeakCentre=2, Height=100, Sigma=0.01;name=Gaussian, PeakCentre=3, Height=100, Sigma=0.01"
+    ws_d = CreateSampleWorkspace("Event","User Defined", myFunc, BankPixelWidth=1, XUnit='dSpacing', XMax=5, BinWidth=0.001, NumEvents=10000, NumBanks=6)
+    for n in range(1,7):
+        MoveInstrumentComponent(ws_d, ComponentName=f'bank{n}', X=1, Y=0, Z=1, RelativePosition=False)
+
+    # Offset the different spectra
+    ws_d = ScaleX(ws_d, Factor=1.05, IndexMin=1, IndexMax=1)
+    ws_d = ScaleX(ws_d, Factor=0.95, IndexMin=2, IndexMax=2)
+    ws_d = ScaleX(ws_d, Factor=1.05, IndexMin=3, IndexMax=5)
+    ws_d = ScaleX(ws_d, Factor=1.02, IndexMin=3, IndexMax=4)
+    ws_d = ScaleX(ws_d, Factor=0.98, IndexMin=4, IndexMax=5)
+    ws_d = Rebin(ws_d, '0,0.001,5')
+    ws = ConvertUnits(ws_d, Target='TOF')
+
+    # Make 2 groups of 3 detectors each
+    groups, _, _, = CreateGroupingWorkspace(InputWorkspace=ws, ComponentName='basic_rect', CustomGroupingString='1-3,4-6')
+
+    # starting DIFC are all the same
+    detectorTable = CreateDetectorTable(ws)
+
+    print("DetID DIFC")
+    for detid, difc in zip(detectorTable.column('Detector ID(s)'), detectorTable.column('DIFC')):
+        print(f'{detid:>5} {difc:.1f}')
+
+.. testoutput:: group_cal
+
+    DetID DIFC
+        1 2208.3
+        2 2208.3
+        3 2208.3
+        4 2208.3
+        5 2208.3
+        6 2208.3
+
+.. testcode:: group_cal
+
+    from Calibration.tofpd.group_calibration import cc_calibrate_groups
+
+    cc_diffcal = cc_calibrate_groups(ws,
+                                     groups,
+                                     DReference=2.0,
+                                     Xmin=1.75,
+                                     Xmax=2.25)
+
+    print("DetID DIFC")
+    for detid, difc in zip(cc_diffcal.column('detid'), cc_diffcal.column('difc')):
+        print(f'{detid:>5} {difc:.1f}')
+
+.. testoutput:: group_cal
+
+    DetID DIFC
+        1 2208.3
+        2 2318.6
+        3 2098.0
+        4 2208.3
+        5 2161.2
+        6 2115.7
+
+.. testcode:: group_cal
+
+    from Calibration.tofpd.group_calibration import pdcalibration_groups
+
+    diffcal, mask = pdcalibration_groups(ws,
+                                         groups,
+                                         cc_diffcal,
+                                         PeakPositions = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0],
+                                         PeakFunction='Gaussian',
+                                         PeakWindow=0.4)
+
+    print("DetID DIFC")
+    for detid, difc in zip(diffcal.column('detid'), diffcal.column('difc')):
+        print(f'{detid:>5} {difc:.1f}')
+
+.. testoutput:: group_cal
+
+    DetID DIFC
+        1 2208.7
+        2 2319.0
+        3 2098.4
+        4 2368.8
+        5 2318.3
+        6 2269.5
+
+The evolution in the calibration can be seen with
+
+.. code::
+
+   import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+   from mantid import plots
+
+   ws_d = Rebin(ws_d, '0.75,0.01,3.5')
+

+   ws_d_after_cc = ConvertUnits(ws, Target='dSpacing')
+   ws_d_after_cc = Rebin(ws_d_after_cc, '0.75,0.01,3.5')
+
+   ApplyDiffCal(ws, CalibrationWorkspace=diffcal)
+   ws_d_after_cc_and_pd = ConvertUnits(ws, Target='dSpacing')
+   ws_d_after_cc_and_pd = Rebin(ws_d_after_cc_and_pd, '0.75,0.01,3.5')

+import sys
